questions.question: For a symmetric matrix $A$ and column vector $v$, what kind of object is $v^TAv$?
Why is the expression $v^TAv$ called quadratic?
options: It can only be evaluated for $v=(1,1)^T$
It is second degree in the coordinates of $v$

questions.question: What does the quadratic form of the identity matrix give?
options: The sum of the entries of $v$ without squares

questions.question: What role do quadratic forms play in classifying symmetric matrices?
options: They define the number of columns
They are used to define definiteness
They determine whether a matrix is row echelon

questions.question: In $v^TAv$, why is $v$ usually treated as a column vector?
options: So that $v^T A v$ has compatible matrix dimensions
So that $A$ becomes a row vector
So that the result is always a $2\times2$ matrix

questions.question: Let $A=I_2$ and $v=(2,-1)^T$. What is $v^TAv$?
For $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$ and $v=(x,y)^T$, what is $v^TAv$?
For $A=\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\0&3\end{pmatrix}$ and $v=(1,2)^T$, compute $v^TAv$.
For $A=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ and $v=(x,y)^T$, what is $v^TAv$?
For $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$ and $v=(3,2)^T$, compute $v^TAv$.
For a symmetric $2\times2$ matrix $A=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\b&c\end{pmatrix}$, why does the cross term in $v^TAv$ become $2bxy$?
options: The two off-diagonal entries both contribute $bxy$
The diagonal entries create all cross terms
The transpose removes one copy of $b$

questions.question: What value does every quadratic form take at the zero vector?
Why does definiteness focus on the sign of $v^TAv$ for many vectors rather than one vector?
options: A single value cannot show whether the form is always positive, negative, or changes sign
The form is undefined for individual vectors, universally and without exception.
Quadratic forms do not have signs

questions.question: For $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&3\end{pmatrix}$ and $v=(x,y)^T$, what is $v^TAv$?
For $A=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ and $v=(2,3)^T$, compute $v^TAv$.
Which symmetric matrix gives the quadratic form $x^2+6xy+4y^2$?
Why can $x^2-y^2$ suggest that $\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$ is not positive definite?
options: The form is always positive except at zero
The form can be negative for vectors such as $(0,1)^T$

questions.question: What information is lost if one only evaluates $v^TAv$ at standard basis vectors?
options: The fact that the result is a scalar, irrespective of the particular case.

questions.question: For $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&3\end{pmatrix}$ and $v=(1,-1)^T$, compute $v^TAv$.
Which symmetric matrix corresponds to $q(x,y,z)=x^2+2xy+4xz+3z^2$?
